description.value: This study investigated the spatial topography of drug-cue reactivity in cocaine, alcohol, and nicotine dependent individuals using a standardized fMRI drug-cue exposure task.

spans.text: The goal of this study was to prospectively investigate the spatial topography of drug-cue reactivity in a large set of individuals dependent on either cocaine, alcohol, or nicotine.

description.value: Data were aggregated from four investigations of non-treatment-seeking individuals dependent on cocaine, alcohol, or nicotine; participants were recruited from the Charleston, SC metropolitan area and underwent screening followed by an MRI scanning session.

spans.text: For this investigation data was aggregated from four separate investigations of drug cue-reactivity performed at the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) from 2012–2017.

name.value: alcohol cues relative to neutral cues

definition.value: Alcohol cues led to a significant increase in BOLD signal relative to neutral cues.

value: In alcohol users (n = 53) alcohol cues led to a significant increase in BOLD signal relative to neutral cues in 1 cluster: Brodmann 24/32, anterior cingulate (1,32,8; 300; p = 0.008) which extended through the MPFC.
The medial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex are the most consistently activated clusters in cocaine cue-reactivity, alcohol cue-reactivity, and cigarette cue-reactivity.

name.value: cigarette cues relative to neutral cues

definition.value: Cigarette cues led to an increase in BOLD signal relative to neutral cues.

value: In cigarette smokers, cigarette cues also led to an increase in BOLD signal in 1 cluster: Brodmann 24/32, anterior cingulate (−1,36,10; 210; p = 0.048) which extended through the MPFC.
The medial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex are the most consistently activated clusters in cocaine cue-reactivity, alcohol cue-reactivity, and cigarette cue-reactivity.

name.value: cocaine cues relative to neutral cues

definition.value: Cocaine cues led to significantly more BOLD signal than neutral cues.

value: In cocaine users (n = 55) cocaine cues led to significantly more BOLD signal than neutral cues in 3 clusters: left Brodmann 6, right Brodmann 44, and left Brodmann 10, ventral MPFC.
The medial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex are the most consistently activated clusters in cocaine cue-reactivity, alcohol cue-reactivity, and cigarette cue-reactivity.
